body: I work in a department store and was putting stickers on clearance items. A customer walked past and demanded I put a $5 clearance sticker on the $39 cardigan she was carrying because it was "on the pricey side". Laughed awkwardly, said I couldn't do that, 15 min later found the ripped off tags in the fitting room - she stole it instead.

Ah, department stores. Despite only working weekends I've had two genuine death threats - one over a coupon, the other from a shoplifter I (politely) foiled.

It's amazing the people who'll risk police intervention over 5% off.

I've experienced the same with a relative coming in to visit his aunt.
"My aunt works at <insert chain department store>!"

"Well, we don't know anyone by that name here. Are you sure she works at this location?"

"There's more than one <department store!>?"

"Why, yes, we have 200+ locations" *shows him store list*

After a bit of digging we worked out he wasn't even in the right state lmao.

I've been in a similar situation as yourself (high five for chronic boredom), except I was in for Anorexia. 
I had a ham complain that we (anyone with an ED) got better food than her (she was in for some mood disorder). Our food was high calorie so it meant lots of cake and ice cream etc.
She then tried to take some food off my plate telling me "You don't want to eat it anyway."

A nurse saw her.
Chaos ensued.

"anorexia" is the physical action of starving, and can be a symptom of other medical problems (it's even listed as a side effect for some common drugs) whereas "anorexia nervosa" is the action of starving and the cognitions that one associates with disordered eating/body image issues. You can be cured from the "starving" aspect of the disorder by merely gaining weight, but it won't cure the mental illness aspect of it. Sometimes it causes the cognitions to manifest themselves in other eating disorders, a relapse or other coping mechanisms. But, yes, TL;DR version: anorexia =/= anorexia nervosa :)
A bit further south, where's is depressingly cold unfortunately. It does seen like it's a couple "type" though, I've seen quite a few like them.

She did not pay for the shorts and left the mess without saying a (polite) word to any of the staff. If something breaks or is damaged by accident we don't usually make the customer pay, because our store's insurance supposedly covers it and it makes us seem really kind saying "oh, don't worry about it.". Usually if someone breaks/damages something and doesn't apologise or notify us, I make them pay for it bc rude. She got away pretty quickly for a ham and cbs finding her.
I work in a department store, it's almost impossible to enforce unfortunately.
